title: The Burrito Chain Story
content:
Let me tell you about a burrito place. Kate was in college up the road, and every time Diane and I visited, there was this little regional burrito chain with a line out the door. Students, nurses coming off shift, construction crews. Cheap, fast, and people kept coming back.

So I did what any good researcher would do—I ate there! Talked to the manager. Counted the lunch line three visits in a row. Found out they were opening a new location every few months.

The analysts I knew? Nobody cared. 'It's just burritos,' they said.

But here's the thing—I could see it. Regular people could see it. The kids eating there could see it before anyone in an office did.

That's the beauty of noticing what's in your own life. You don't need a terminal full of screens. You need eyes and curiosity. Then you do the homework.
